extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, review administrators, and institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Policy and guidance governing how NIH grant and contract applications are evaluated, including legal/regulatory requirements, reviewer responsibilities (confidentiality, conflict of interest), review criteria, scoring, appeals, and special-topic considerations (human subjects, data sharing, rigor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal framework governing NIH peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH peer review is governed by a legal framework of federal Acts and Regulations including: PHS Act 42 U.S.C. 289a (requires two levels of peer review), PHS Act 42 U.S.C. 284a (authorizes appropriate scientific and technical peer review through advisory committees), the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), the Government in the Sunshine Act (directing when advisory committee meetings may be closed or partially closed to the public), and 42 CFR 52h (Scientific Peer Review of Research Grant Applications and Research and Development Contract Projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes/regulations establish mandatory structural and procedural requirements for how applications must be evaluated and how peer review meetings are conducted (e.g., two-level review, advisory committee governance, meeting openness rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for two levels of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PHS Act 42 U.S.C. 289a, applications must undergo two levels of peer review for a grant award to be made by the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly defines the first-level (initial scientific/technical review) and second-level (advisory council/board) review stages; both stages have distinct responsibilities and criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review integrity and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review is a core policy area, with notices such as 'Maintaining Security and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review: Rules, Responsibilities and Possible Consequences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must protect the confidentiality of application materials and deliberations; security requirements and potential consequences for breaches are specified in policy notices and FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of generative AI technologies in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technologies is Prohibited for the NIH Peer Review Process (policy notice NOT-OD-23-149).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are explicitly forbidden from employing generative AI tools as part of the NIH peer review process; related FAQs address confidentiality and permitted/unpermitted uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing conflict of interest (COI) in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing Conflict of Interest in NIH Peer Review of Grants and Contracts is a central policy area, including policy notices such as the Advance Notice: Revised Policy for Managing Conflict of Interest in the Initial Peer Review of NIH Grant and Cooperative Agreement Applications (NOT-OD-13-010) and related FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies provide rules and procedures for identifying, disclosing, and handling conflicts (including disclosure of other support/foreign components), recusal, and board-level management of COI to protect review integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria and considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer Review Criteria and Considerations provides the substantive evaluation dimensions reviewers should use when assessing applications (and is linked alongside the Simplified Peer Review Framework and other guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This resource contains the evaluative criteria (and special considerations) that inform reviewers' written critiques and scores; see the Consolidated List of Reviewer Documents for detailed step-by-step reviewer guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified Peer Review Framework for Research Project Grants (RPGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy notice and guidance on the Simplified Review Framework for Most Research Project Grants (NOT-OD-24-010) and associated applicant and reviewer guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes an implementation of simplified review/criteria for many RPGs (changes to review structure, criteria emphasis, and reviewer instructions); detailed implementation and FAQs are provided in the linked notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring procedures for first-level peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring in First Level Peer Review and related policy notices (e.g., 'Enhancing Peer Review: The NIH Announces New Scoring Procedures for Evaluation of Research Applications' NOT-OD-09-024) describe how reviewers must assign scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and FAQs explain the scoring scale, interpretation of score values, and how scores relate to overall impact and funding decisions; reviewers should follow updated scoring procedures in the notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process for first-level peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and notices on Appeals in First Level Peer Review describe the mechanism by which applicants may appeal initial peer review outcomes (NOT-OD-11-064).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and applicant-facing documents outline grounds for appeal, timelines, and next steps (including 'Applicant Guidance: Next Steps').

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of NIH peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: A published set of Core Values of NIH Peer Review (PDF) articulates the foundational principles that should guide reviewers and review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core values (e.g., fairness, balance, expertise, confidentiality, transparency, integrity) are instructional expectations reviewers should embody; the PDF provides detail on these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities and stepwise guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated List of Reviewer Documents and 'Information for Reviewers' provide reviewer guidance for individual steps of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These materials include procedural instructions, templates, and checklists reviewers should use when preparing critiques, declaring conflicts, recusing, and documenting scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects and clinical-trial specific review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH provides guidance on 'Human Subjects in Peer Review' and 'Clinical Trial-Specific Review Criteria' to address evaluation of studies involving human participants and clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must evaluate protections for human subjects, ethical safeguards, data monitoring plans, informed consent, and trial-specific design and analysis considerations; special review pathways and forms (e.g., Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information Form) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and resources for 'Rigor and Reproducibility in Grant Applications' and 'Principles and Guidelines for Publishing Preclinical Research' set expectations for methodological rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess experimental design, reproducibility measures, statistical approaches, and plans to ensure robust, replicable findings; training and resources are available for applicants and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and sharing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Data Management and Sharing Policy (DMS) and associated resources (writing a DMS plan, budgeting, repository selection) set requirements for how investigators must manage and share data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include appropriate data management & sharing plans; reviewers and program staff consider these plans during review and for award compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion policies for human subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion Policies (e.g., Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Inclusion Across the Lifespan, Valid Analysis for NIH-defined Phase III Clinical Trials) specify participant inclusion and analysis requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether study populations and analysis plans meet inclusion requirements and whether subgroup analyses and power are adequate for NIH-defined trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of other support, foreign components, and foreign interference expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for Disclosure of Other Support, Foreign Components and Conflicts of Interest, together with materials on 'About Foreign Interference' and processes for handling allegations, inform disclosure and integrity obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must fully disclose other support and foreign affiliations/components; reviewers and administrators must follow policies for detecting and handling potential foreign influence or undisclosed support, per NIH notices and procedures.
